name: Gule
world_status: accessible description is silent on stress

earlier_scan.source_named: Extinct; only 19th-c. wordlists (Marno 1874, Lejean 1865) per Glottolog.

sources.citation: Glottolog 5.x languoid page gule1241 (Hammarström et al.).
sources.note: No descriptive references at all (Glottolog lists no grammar, sketch or phonology); classification note: evidence for Koman membership 'so far insufficient' (Bender 1983; Güldemann 2018); AES extinct.

sources.citation: Wiktionary. Appendix: Gule word lists (transcribing Seligmann 1912 and Evans-Pritchard 1932).
sources.access_detail: a copy the project holds (available on request)
sources.note: Secondary transcription only; reproduces Seligmann's acutes and Evans-Pritchard's breve/macron marks (E-P forms show no acutes); no statement about stress.

sources.citation: Seligmann, Brenda Z. 1911-1912. Note on two languages spoken in the Sennar Province of the Anglo-Egyptian Sudan. Zeitschrift für Kolonialsprachen 2: 297-308.
sources.access_detail: a copy the project holds (available on request)
sources.note: Nothing. The only first-hand grammatical notes on Gule (~80 words, plural/adjective/numeral/verb/preposition sentences, pp. 299-308). The transcription carries unexplained acute accents on many forms (p. 300 mítagamal 'hand', kobédĭn; p. 301 kósan 'spear', gărăwáig 'man', indéluk 'many'; p. 303 dĕdín 'one', dĕssú 'two', dĭnāmú 'three', dĭkássabit 'four', dŭbŭ́ĭt 'five', dĕlódĭn 'six', debḗdig 'eight', dĕmadídin 'nine') but no key says what the acute marks, and there is no sentence about accent, stress or tone anywhere in the article.

sources.citation: Zöppritz, Karl (ed.). 1877. E. de Pruyssenaere's Reisen und Forschungen im Gebiete des Weissen und Blauen Nil. Petermanns Geographische Mittheilungen, Ergänzungsheft 50-51 (Heft 2, Anhang: Kleines Vocabular des Ingasana, sowie einiger Fung-Wörter).
sources.access_detail: a copy the project holds (available on request)
sources.note: Nothing. A dozen Fung words (Sandale beg, Wind mugus, Armband soward; wo 'ich', nan 'du', anok 'er') and numerals 1-10 (din, su, num, kasabet, bug, lodin, laso, bedik, mandidin, dörköbu); refers the reader to Lejean, Voyage aux deux Nils p. 177 and Marno pp. 481 ff. No stress remark.

sources.citation: Marno, Ernst. 1874. Reisen im Gebiete des blauen und weissen Nil.. 1869 bis 1873. Wien: Carl Gerold's Sohn. Anhang II 'Kleine Vocabularien der Fungi-, Tabi-, Bertat- und Nuehr-Sprache', pp. 481-495.
sources.access_detail: a copy the project holds (available on request)
sources.note: Nothing. Landscape German-gloss wordlist with a 'Fungi (von Gbl. Gule)' column (p. 481 viewed: abbar, alà, agad, nagad, nilé, ibibis, rátona, bunj..); no accent key, no remark on stress; the narrative (p. ~410) only says the author 'legte ein kleines Vocabular der Fungi- und Tabisprache an'.

Nothing on phonology; its value is the citation of Zamponi, Raoul. 2026. Gule. Routledge World Languages (ISBN 9781041032298, academia.edu preprint page 126721374, which could not be reached by automated download).

sources.citation: Zamponi, Raoul. 2026/c2027. Gule. Routledge World Languages. London/New York: Routledge. 162 pp. ISBN 9781041032298. Ch. 1 'Phonology'.
sources.tag: likely states stress; not yet obtained
sources.note: The first and only systematic phonology/grammar of Gule, reconstructed from Seligmann's notes and a 1966 Wendy James recording; its phonology chapter is where any statement about Gule stress/accent (and an interpretation of Seligmann's acute accents) will be. Supersedes everything else.
